method: QUOTED UNDER A 200-WORD BUDGET (195 words used), from Cancer Council Australia 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia' v0.20 (published 2023-09-25), retrieved 2026-09-23 as MAGICapp JSON. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read, NOT openly licensed. Cancer Council Australia's guideline FAQ: fair dealing needs only correct citation; reproducing 'more than 200 words or figures/tables' needs permission from guidelines@cancer.org.au. So quotes here are capped at 200 words per source guideline (enforced by the generator) and tables were stripped from the retrieved text before quoting, so none can be quoted.

claims.claim: **In cirrhosis, offer 6-monthly HCC surveillance — ultrasound, with or without alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) — to people who are willing and suitable to receive HCC treatment.**
claims.source_text: In people with cirrhosis who are willing(a) and suitable(b) to receive HCC treatment, offer … 6-monthly surveillance for HCC (using ultrasound, with or without alpha-fetoprotein testing)
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not routinely offer HCC surveillance to people with limited projected life expectancy.**
claims.source_text: not routinely offer surveillance for HCC … for people who have limited projected life expectancy
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HCV-related cirrhosis with a sustained virologic response: still offer 6-monthly surveillance** (ultrasound, with or without AFP).
claims.source_text: In people with HCV-related cirrhosis who achieve a sustained virologic response to treatment, offer … 6-monthly surveillance for HCC (using ultrasound, with or without alpha-fetoprotein testing)
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HCV with F3 (non-cirrhotic) fibrosis and a sustained virologic response: do not routinely offer HCC surveillance** — but monitor for progression to cirrhosis.
claims.source_text: In people with HCV and F3 fibrosis (non-cirrhotic)# … not routinely offer surveillance for HCC … should be monitored* for progression to cirrhosis
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MAFLD/NAFLD without cirrhosis: monitor for progression to cirrhosis.**
claims.source_text: People with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease/non-alcoholic fatty liver disease without cirrhosis … should be monitored* for progression to cirrhosis
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with chronic HBV: consider 6-monthly surveillance from age 50 or more** — or earlier with a family history of HCC, or from age 40 or more with a high-risk HBV genotype.
claims.source_text: In Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people … with chronic HBV infection, consider offering … 6-monthly surveillance for HCC (using ultrasound, with or without alpha-fetoprotein testing) … if age ≥ 50 years … if there is a family history of HCC1 or if age ≥ 40 with a high-risk HBV genotype2
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asian or Pacific background with chronic HBV: consider 6-monthly surveillance for males aged 40 or more and females aged 50 or more.**
claims.source_text: In people of Asian or Pacific background … with chronic HBV infection, consider offering … 6-monthly surveillance for HCC (using ultrasound, with or without alpha-fetoprotein testing) … males ≥ 40 years of age females ≥ 50 years of age
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Clinical practice guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance for people at high risk in Australia', v0.20, published 2023-09-25, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/E83abn, retrieved 2026-09-23
